sources.entry: Tomoru - Live bilingual subtitles for streams, anime, games, and meetings, plus instant screen text translation — works offline on your Mac or in the cloud, with glossaries that keep character names right. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/ACAne0320/Tomoru) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Tomoru
summary.one_liner: Tomoru is an open-source desktop app that captures system audio and shows floating bilingual subtitles for streams, anime, games, and meetings, with on-screen text translation.
use_cases: Watching foreign-language live streams with subtitles
Translating game dialogue in real time
Following meetings and online lectures in another language
Translating text on screen such as signs or chat in a video
summary.what_it_does: Tomoru captures the computer's system audio output (not the microphone) and generates floating subtitles with bilingual text in real time. The subtitle window stays on top, can be dragged and resized, and can be locked for click-through, with automatic hiding during screen recording or streaming. Speech recognition and translation can run fully offline on the local machine or use a free cloud translation option or a user-supplied LLM API. A per-show glossary corrects names and terms, and a select-to-translate hotkey translates text on screen. The page lists 31 languages.
notable: Captures system audio only and never requests microphone access
Fully local offline speech recognition and translation option
Glossary of proper nouns to fix mishears and keep consistent names
Select-screen-area hotkey translates on-screen text, including with local models
caveats: Unsigned installers may trigger a system warning that must be bypassed manually
Cloud translation and custom LLM API use depend on external services; the page does not detail costs
Requires macOS 26 or later on Apple chips, Windows 11 x64, or Linux x64 per the page
